evidence:
APPLICABILITY. The brief has many interactive and time-varying requirements. instruction.md:5 asks for live board updates within 15 s without a reload, keeping the open card, the note being typed and the cursor. instruction.md:3 asks for moves shown at once and put back with a reason if refused. instruction.md:7 asks for the newest 30 messages first, pulling in earlier ones without losing place, arrivals while scrolled up, and drafts kept across a conversation switch, a reload and a sign-out. The same rules appear in hireops_rules.md:84-88, 121-129 and 145-182. Theming and phone layout are explicitly not required: instruction.md:11 says 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout', and visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' The task correctly dropped the template's 390x844 mobile legs (template tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23 and visual/prompt.md:29), so no resize or toggle step is owed.

EXERCISED BY ACTION, NOT FIRST PAINT. Every interactive or time-varying requirement is graded by acting on the page.
- Waits and live updates. functional/prompt.md:29 and polish/prompt.md:18 define one timed observation run inside a single browser_run_code_unsafe call: the other person acts in an independent context; t0 is recorded only after that action succeeds; the DOM is polled every 500 ms for 15000 ms without clicking, typing, scrolling or reloading the watched page; the call returns {triggerOk, met, ms}. An attempt is void only if it fails before t0, a void attempt may be repeated at most twice, and met:false is final. A negative is watched for the full 15000 ms and confirmed again in a fresh context. This protocol is used by hro_two_people (functional/judge.toml:95, Mei's move and new card), hro_messaging (:158, reply arrival), hro_long_thread (:176, the notice while scrolled up) and hro_unread_seen (:185, counts, totals and seen marks, plus the negative where only the Observer opens). That satisfies Colderwater lessons 7 and 14 for every similar criterion, not just one.
- Keeping state through a live update. hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:53) makes the board scroll (up to twelve cards) and scrolls it partway, opens a card's details, clicks into the note box, types, and reads scrollTop. A colleague then moves another card. The judge reads that the details are still open, the note is exact, document.activeElement is unchanged and scroll is within 2 px, then types more to prove the text appends. hro_pol_live_thread (:62) and hro_long_thread own the at-newest and scrolled-up cases, with ownership split explicitly between them.
- Clicks and keyboard. hro_moves (:77) uses ordinary non-drag controls and checks the first look after the action. hro_interview_places (:104) checks the card is put back, the reason is shown, and document.activeElement is inside the card. hro_messaging checks Shift+Enter and Enter, and that the box is empty and focused after sending. hro_pol_earlier_place (polish :71) compares getBoundingClientRect().top before and after loading earlier messages. hro_drafts (:167) switches conversation, goes to the Board and reloads. hro_pol_session_resume (:89) signs out in a second tab and then presses Enter. hro_pol_failed_send (:80) uses a route abort or setOffline. app_context.md:75-77 says to hold a modifier key during the click (lesson 8). Every prompt has a 'Report every step' rule where a skipped step fails (functional/prompt.md:31-33, polish/prompt.md:20-22; lesson 9).

COUNTEREXAMPLE ATTEMPTS. (a) An app that refreshes the board only on window focus or on the user's next click fails the timed protocol, because the watched page is never clicked and met:false is final. (b) An app that re-renders the board or thread and resets scroll, closes the details or drops focus fails hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread or hro_long_thread on numeric reads. (c) An app polling every 30-60 s passes polish (60 s watch; speed is graded elsewhere) but fails the 15 s legs of hro_two_people, hro_messaging and hro_unread_seen. (d) A conforming alternative using SSE, sockets or polling is accepted (rules :129). (e) A conforming infinite-scroll 'pull earlier' can be reached by scrolling; there is a small ambiguity only in hro_pol_earlier_place (see residual risk 4). I found no criterion that scores a still first paint.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE. I re-hashed every raw-evidence-index.json entry: all 8 artifact sha256 values match, and every matching_source_files hash matches the frozen task bytes. workspace.json (page_errors []) records scripted golden observations that include 'live board ... open card, note draft and focus kept' (arrival_ms 799) and 'conversation ... arrival while reading keeps draft, focus and scroll and is not marked read until viewed'. This is a scripted golden harness, not a configured judge run. The index scope says full configured grading is absent, so whether the GLM judge actually performs these waits and clicks within its budget is NOT EXERCISED.

RESIDUAL RISKS (why risk=true).
(1) No configured judge run shows the judge completing the timed single-call observations within the playwright-mcp code-runner limits and the 600 s / 900 s timeouts. These include the 60 s watches with an independent-context sign-in inside one browser_run_code_unsafe call.
(2) The golden live-board script (workspace.cjs:387-404) never scrolls the board, so it does not measure the 2 px scroll leg that hro_pol_live_board grades, and it triggers the colleague's move through the API. The at-newest live-thread leg graded by hro_pol_live_thread is also not scripted directly.
(3) Minor: hro_two_people tests the stale-move refusal by a fetch replay, so on-screen catch-up after a stale move sent from the UI is not exercised. The bar accepts the colleague's name in the response, which hireops_rules.md:78-82 allows.
(4) Minor: hro_pol_earlier_place does not say what to do if the app auto-loads earlier messages when the view reaches the top, so a judge could misread a second deliberate scroll as a jump.
Neither (3) nor (4) is a demonstrated wrong grade, so the row passes on design.
suggested_fix: No blocking fix. Optional: (a) extend the golden harness to scroll the board partway, assert the 2 px leg, and script the at-newest live-thread leg; (b) state in hro_pol_earlier_place that an auto-load triggered by reaching the top counts as bringing in earlier messages, and measure from the message noted before it fired; (c) get a configured judge run showing the timed single-call observations complete.
